# SDK status, original build intent, and plan drift
SDK status, original build intent, and plan drift
As of: October 9, 2026, America/Detroit. Author: Codex side conversation.
SDK status, original build intent, and plan drift

Scope: a documentary checkpoint of the existing SDK, relevant AI Money core packages, current proof, and outstanding build work. This document does not change the SDK, release artifacts, canonical gap CSV, build plan, agent profiles, hooks, or Google Sheet. Cursor remains the implementation owner. No installation, provider call, paid inference, deployment, or new test execution was performed to write this report.

**The SDK is a working, versioned toolkit for building and maintaining the agent system. The full intended agent system is not yet demonstrated end to end.** SDK 1.5.1 is the latest independently verified release located in the inspected records. Its exact source is `157e2ae7d0d48922a6fadaf972583bdcc8f6132b`, on `wt/connect-integration-20261009`, in the [connect-integration worktree](/Users/alexlobaito/Documents/Codex/master-agent-operations-sdk-worktrees/connect-integration). [S1], [S2]

The SDK now has useful building blocks: editable files and configuration, bounded process recipes, scoped agent profiles, Composio shared-skill validation, direct Connect access, durable receipts and recovery, remote-file operations, memory recall, and typed decision interfaces. Their proof levels differ. A successful local SDK test does not establish that Hermes loaded the package, selected a skill, received a recalled memory, or completed a delegated job.

The relevant AI Money goal is **adopting the useful mechanisms in the core packages already collected**, especially Persona OS, Smart Orchestrator, Codex Model Router, and their supporting profile/handoff material. It is not acquiring every community resource or reproducing Bo's inaccessible private configuration. The original plan already says the private configuration is not a prerequisite. [S3]

1. **Source to implementation:** for each relevant course-package feature, identify our exact implementation, adaptation, or remaining work.
2. **Implementation to live agents:** prove the behavior on Javar and Javante, with correct accounts, memory, task/result delivery, independent checks, and recovery.

This is Alex's custom **Master Agent Operations SDK**, implemented in Python. An SDK is a reusable software toolkit: it gives Codex and other authorized callers consistent operations instead of making them reconstruct shell commands, connector calls, account selection, backup logic, and verification for every job.

The common implementation is available through a Python facade, JSON command-line interfaces, and a stdio MCP interface. The broad master capability registry can be extended; Javar, Javante, and later agents receive narrower profiles from the same implementation. The common toolkit is not itself a complete Hermes profile, a deployed agent team, a replacement model, or a CRM sales-agent policy. [S4]

8. How the SDK was supposed to make this faster
## 8. How the SDK was supposed to make this faster
8. How the SDK was supposed to make this faster
The speed mechanism is **reuse of deterministic operations and context**, not simply adding more agents or more tools. [S3]
8. How the SDK was supposed to make this faster

| Repeated work today | Intended reusable SDK path |
|---|---|
| Rediscover the computer, profile, account and file paths | Named target bindings and capability profiles |
| Handcraft each edit and backup | One inspect → preimage/backup → revision check → apply → independent readback → restore sequence |
| Re-explain permission and skill rules | Registered shared workflow, pinned content, current schema, named account |
| Rebuild task prompts after every interruption | Typed task brief, source/context references, stable task identity and persisted checkpoint |
| Paste large histories into every worker | Bounded context/recall blocks with prov
8. How the SDK was supposed to make this faster

enance and exact delivery approval |
| Ask the worker what happened and trust its summary | Structured receipts plus independent acceptance of the real output |
| Invent a new integration for every host | Common operation contracts with narrow Codex/Hermes/Orgo adapters |
| Reapply the same skill/configuration manually | Versioned delivery recipe, target readback, fresh-session test and rollback |
8. How the SDK was supposed to make this faster

Example of the intended build use: choose a relevant Persona OS workspace behavior → locate the exact source template → map it to the existing Hermes-owned file → apply through the SDK with backup/revision checks → activate on the canary → test the behavior → retain the result and rollback path. The reusable machinery should make the second feature cheaper to implement than the first.
8. How the SDK was supposed to make this faster

**Not measured yet:** percentage token savings, a 2× build-speed improvement, or equivalent claims. Measure the same bounded task before/after, including research/setup, implementation, review, retries, and final acceptance. A faster runner or smaller response is not the whole-workflow result.
